problem: Earlier reviews (Cadena et al. SLAM survey, Fraundorfer & Scaramuzza on VO, Paden et al. on motion planning) cover classical geometric vSLAM and planning. No review jointly covered learning-based monocular perception (depth, ego-motion, image enhancement, detection/segmentation fused with vSLAM) and RL/DRL-based visual navigation for autonomous systems.
motivation: Classical vSLAM depends on strong assumptions: static scenes and photometric consistency. As a result it fails in low-texture, dynamic, night-time and cross-weather/season conditions, and monocular systems suffer from scale ambiguity. Deep learning can relax these assumptions, and (deep) RL offers end-to-end navigation without hand-built planners. The survey therefore organizes where and how learning improves perception and navigation.
key_idea: Organize the learning-era literature into (i) geometric vSLAM as the baseline, (ii) deep monocular depth/ego-motion estimation, (iii) hybrid DL+vSLAM systems and (iv) RL/DRL visual navigation, then distill the ways learning plugs into traditional pipelines and the open challenges.
insight: Learning improves traditional frameworks in two main ways. The first is enhancing inputs, e.g., night-to-day GAN translation (multi-frame GAN) or lighting-invariant feature maps (GN-Net) fed to direct/feature SLAM. The second is embedding learned modules, e.g., CNN depth as the initial guess refined by LSD-SLAM (CNN-SLAM), a pose network replacing DSO's constant-motion model, or D3VO's depth/pose/uncertainty networks. The taxonomy table of depth/ego-motion methods shows a trend: from supervised to unsupervised view-reconstruction training, toward multi-task coupling with optical/scene flow and segmentation, and toward multi-sensor (IMU) fusion. On navigation, the survey highlights three points: auxiliary tasks (depth prediction, loop closure, reward prediction) speed up RL; modular mapping/decision/planning frameworks generalize better than raw end-to-end DRL; and noisy vSLAM maps or domain randomization help sim-to-real transfer. All of this is qualitative, drawn from cited works, with no new ablations.
method: Geometric vSLAM taxonomy (Table I): 2003–2021 systems (MonoSLAM, PTAM, DTAM, LSD-SLAM, SVO, ORB-SLAM1/2/3, DSO, VINS-Mono, etc.) classified by filtering vs optimization, direct/semi-direct/feature-based, dense/semi-dense/sparse map and sensor, plus the failure modes of each family.

Learning-based monocular depth review: supervised, stereo-semi-supervised and monocular-unsupervised (view reconstruction) methods. Covers open issues: edge-aware smoothness/surface normals, dynamic objects (auto-masking, semantic masking), novel cameras, night-time depth (DeFeat-Net, adversarial day–night feature adaptation, CycleGAN adaptation).

Learning-based ego-motion review: PoseNet, DeepVO-style RNNs, memory/refining modules, graph NN view graphs, online meta-learning, Conv-LSTM long-term constraints, flow-based fundamental-matrix pose, and end-to-end VIO (VINet, attention-based selective fusion). Summarized in Table II by training data, supervision type and tasks.

DL + vSLAM hybrids: learned depth priors (CNN-SLAM, DVSO, CNN-SVO, DeepFactors), learned pose priors/corrections (DSO init, D3VO, pose correction, DROID-SLAM), image enhancement for HDR/night, detection/segmentation for dynamic-feature removal (Detect-SLAM, DS-SLAM, SOF), object-based scale recovery, and semantic mapping (SemanticFusion, CRF-based maps).

RL visual navigation: the classical map-based / map-building / mapless taxonomy, Q-learning with compact state spaces, auxiliary-task RL (UNREAL, Mirowski et al.), and a brief treatment of VLN (seq2seq, RCM + SIL, dual-attention).

DRL visual navigation: value-based (DQN, dueling/double DQN), policy-based (DDPG, NAF, asynchronous DDPG, AutoRL), actor-critic (A3C target-driven navigation in AI2-THOR, SAC), LSTM memory for city-scale street navigation, and sim-to-real via domain randomization, vSLAM maps and modular frameworks.

Challenges/directions: accurate, robust and real-time perception; geometry/knowledge-graph priors; NeRF-based map representation; multi-sensor fusion; sparse rewards; sample cost; sim-to-real; transferability; multi-modal/multi-task RL.

setting.observation: N/A (survey; focus on monocular RGB perception, with some RGB-D/stereo/IMU works covered)
setting.simulator: N/A (survey; mentions AI2-THOR and KITTI for surveyed works)

numbers_note: Survey paper: no experimental results. Tables I and II are qualitative taxonomies (checkmarks for method type, supervision and tasks) with no benchmark metrics.
results: No quantitative results. The main deliverables are two taxonomy tables (geometric vSLAM 2003–2021; deep monocular depth/ego-motion 2014–2021) and a narrative review. The survey concludes that DL modules improve the robustness, scale recovery and dynamic/night-time performance of monocular vSLAM, and that DRL navigation shows good efficiency and transferability but still faces sparse rewards, high sample cost and a sim-to-real gap.
limitations: Navigation coverage is thin and dated relative to embodied-navigation research. Habitat-era PointNav/ObjectNav/ImageNav benchmarks and modular map-based agents are essentially absent. VLN gets one paragraph, which confusingly attributes RCM/SIL to Chaplot et al.'s dual-attention paragraph.
No quantitative cross-method comparison: no KITTI depth/odometry or navigation benchmark tables, so readers cannot compare methods numerically.
Perception review focuses on monocular, driving-oriented (KITTI-style) settings, and the RL navigation review is broad but shallow.
